# Prism (46 endpoints)

## Endpoints

|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /lookup | `url` | 1-5 | Universal post/product URL dispatcher: any post, video, product or repo link → the right detail endpoint's unified response. |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /lookup — 1-5cr

Sniffs the platform + endpoint from a URL and returns that endpoint's unified data, with no surcharge. You pay the resolved endpoint's own cost. The join key the whole API runs on is `url`. Takes an ITEM link (a post, video, pin, tweet, repo, product or track), not a profile or channel link, on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X/Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest, Reddit, Threads, Rumble, Truth Social, GitHub, Amazon and Spotify. The `resolved` block names the platform, endpoint, and archetype of the response so agents know the shape that follows; `legs[]` reports the dispatched call's status, cost, and latency.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Absolute http(s) URL of a single post, video, product or repo. Profile, channel and storefront URLs are NOT accepted: use that platform's own `/profile` endpoint for those.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV of optional flags to forward verbatim to the resolved endpoint (e.g. `trim`). Each member must be an optional param of that endpoint.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/lookup?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /comments — 2-200cr

Give it any TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Reddit, Hacker News, or Instagram post URL and it harvests every top-level comment (paginated to the end) with replies nested where the platform supports it (TikTok, YouTube, Facebook). Reddit and Hacker News return their whole nested thread. Instagram comes back top-level only, because its comment source has no reply leg to walk; its replies are still reachable, one call per parent comment, from `GET /v1/instagram/post/comment/replies` (post `url` plus the parent `comment_id`, cursor-paged, 1 credit a call). Every Instagram comment carries `engagement.replies`, so call it only for the comments whose count is above zero. Pass `sort=top` to get the most-liked comments first (ranked by `engagement.likes`): ideal for pulling the top comments on a high-volume post; pair it with `limit` to cap how many you get back (e.g. `sort=top&max=500&limit=200` scans ~500 and returns the top 200). YouTube sorts upstream so its top set is exact; other platforms are sorted across the scanned set. Metered at 1 credit per internal page call (minimum 2): `sort`/`limit` never change the price, which always follows pages scanned (`max`). Instagram is the exception: an Instagram post URL is a flat 5 credits per call whatever `max` and `replies` you pass, because that source returns the comment set in one mobile-upstream call rather than by page. Returns sync JSON, or a typed SSE stream when you send `Accept: text/event-stream`: a `page` chunk lands as each page settles. The `next_cursor` is one opaque token that resumes every leg; `legs[]` reports each page's status, cost, and latency.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 2-200 credits a call — budget the 200 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 2-200 (metered): 1 credit per comment page scanned, except on Instagram, where a post URL is a flat 5 credits whatever `max` and `replies` you pass

**Parameters**

- `url`: Absolute http(s) URL of the post whose comments to harvest.
- `max` *(optional)*: Stop after roughly this many top-level comments (1-5000, default 1000). Whole pages are returned, so the actual count can slightly exceed this. Drives billing and, for `sort=top`, the depth of the ranking scan.
- `replies` *(optional)*: Expand replies for comments that have them, where the platform supports it (default true; TikTok/YouTube/Facebook). Reddit and Hacker News always return their whole nested thread and ignore it. On Instagram it has no effect and is never charged for: take `comment.id` from any comment whose `engagement.replies` is above zero and call `GET /v1/instagram/post/comment/replies` instead. Pair with `replies=false` when you only want the top comments.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Opaque composite cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor` to resume harvesting.
- `sort` *(optional)*: `recent` (default: natural order) or `top` (most-liked first, ranked by each comment's like count). With `top`, the response adds `sorted_by: "likes_desc"`. On Instagram, `top` returns the platform's own ranked head (`sorted_by: "popular"`) rather than a re-sort, and that head is finite: use the default `recent` to harvest a whole Instagram thread.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Cap on how many top-level comments to return after sorting/scanning (1-5000, defaults to `max`). Truncates only the returned set, never what was scanned or billed. The response reports `returned`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/comments?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /brand-mentions — 50cr

Fans out to content_analysis summary, phrase-trends, and search in parallel, then folds them into one envelope with a computed volume/sentiment trajectory (OLS slope + a noise-aware direction) and an optional LLM digest (`include=digest`). Sentiment is NLP-derived (content_analysis), and mention freshness lags the live web by days: `computed.sentiment_provenance` names the exact leg the split came from and states that the values are third-party model probabilities, not human-labelled ground truth, so you can audit them against `recent_mentions` yourself. Each `recent_mentions` row also carries a judged `mention` label (nullable): `about_brand` (a probability, so a name collision such as the notion of time for Notion reads near 0), `sentiment_level` 0 to 4 toward that brand, `sarcastic`, `aspect` and `first_hand`; `computed.mention_labels` counts them in code (rows not about the brand with their ids, positive/neutral/negative, and negative mentions by aspect) and is scoped to that recent sample, not to `total_count`. If the labels cannot be produced the rest of the response is unchanged and `_warnings` says `mention_labels_unavailable`. The price is the same either way. The `computed` block carries stable keys + a `methodology_version` so a monitor can diff runs. `legs[]` reports each leg's status, cost, and latency; if one of the three data legs fails the call still returns a degraded result, and a strict-majority failure refunds half.

**Parameters**

- `keyword`: The brand or term to track. Wrap in quotes for exact-phrase semantics.
- `date_from`: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD). Required by the trend leg.
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the latest crawl.
- `date_group` *(optional)*: Trend bucket size: day (default), week, or month.
- `page_type` *(optional)*: Optional surface filter: ecommerce, news, blogs, message-boards, or organization.
- `include` *(optional)*: Set `digest` to add an LLM narrative summary leg.
- `brand_description` *(optional)*: Optional one-line description of the brand, used to tell it apart from other things with the same name.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/brand-mentions?keyword=<keyword>&date_from=<date_from>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /demand-signals — 30cr

Reads up to four consumer-demand axes in parallel: app-review velocity (the freshest public channel), web mention slope (content_analysis phrase-trends, a real stateless time-series), Reddit sort=new velocity, and Amazon review-count level, and fuses them into published demand-index inputs (never an opaque score; every weight, anchor, and observation window is disclosed). v1 is an honest one-shot level+slope: three of the four axes are point-in-time rates/levels whose true week-over-week deltas need a monitor (the methodology block names them). Supply google_play_id/app_store_id for the app-review axis. legs[] reports each leg status, cost, and latency; a strict-majority leg failure refunds half. Flat 30 credits.

**Parameters**

- `keyword`: The brand or product to nowcast. Drives the mention, Reddit, and Amazon legs.
- `google_play_id` *(optional)*: Google Play package name (e.g. com.spotify.music) for the app-review velocity axis.
- `app_store_id` *(optional)*: Apple App Store numeric id for the app-review velocity axis.
- `signals` *(optional)*: CSV subset of app_reviews,mentions,reddit,commerce (default all). app_reviews is dropped when no app id is supplied.
- `amazon_query` *(optional)*: Override the Amazon product-search term if it differs from the brand.
- `country` *(optional)*: Location for the app-review legs (default United States); a 2-letter code is also applied to the Amazon leg.
- `date_from` *(optional)*: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD) for the mention-slope leg. Defaults to 30 days ago.
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Reviews per store for the velocity computation (1-600, default 150).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/demand-signals?keyword=<keyword>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /campaign — 35cr

Fans out to content_analysis phrase-trends (pre/during/post windows), search/everywhere (consuming items_by_source for real per-platform engagement, not the capped fused items), and tiktok/youtube search for amplifier discovery, then folds them into a lift report (volume lift %, sustained-floor check, ranked amplifiers). YouTube amplifiers are undated in fusion: pass include=amplifier_dates to date the top ones via direct youtube/video calls. Supply hashtag OR phrase plus window_start; window_end defaults to today. Each amplifier also carries a judged `mention` label (is the post about the campaign, or the `brand` you name), and `top_amplifiers_about_brand` repeats the engagement ranking without the posts judged to be about something else; `top_amplifiers` is unchanged. legs[] reports each leg; losing the CA timeline or the everywhere engagement spine refunds half. Flat 35 credits.

**Parameters**

- `window_start` *(optional)*: Campaign launch date (YYYY-MM-DD): the pre/during boundary. Optional; defaults to 30 days ago.
- `window_end` *(optional)*: Campaign end date (YYYY-MM-DD): the during/post boundary. Defaults to today.
- `pre_days` *(optional)*: Baseline days before window_start for lift measurement (1-90, default 14).
- `post_days` *(optional)*: Days after window_end for the post window (0-90, default 14; 0 = no post window).
- `include` *(optional)*: Set amplifier_dates to date YouTube amplifiers via direct youtube/video calls (undated in fusion).
- `brand` *(optional)*: Optional brand the amplifier posts are judged against. Defaults to the hashtag or phrase.
- `brand_description` *(optional)*: Optional one-line description of the brand or campaign, used to tell it apart from other things with the same name.
- `hashtag` / `phrase` — at least one required.
  - `hashtag`: The campaign hashtag (with or without #). One of hashtag or phrase is required. (one of: hashtag, phrase; at least one required)
  - `phrase`: A campaign slogan/phrase instead of a hashtag. One of hashtag or phrase is required. (one of: hashtag, phrase; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/campaign?hashtag=<hashtag>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /ai-visibility — 2-1605cr

Probes your brand (and competitors) across grounded-answer AI engines (Perplexity Sonar + Grok) over a prompt set with N reruns, then reports the share of runs your brand appeared in per engine (appearance-%, never volatile rank) plus a ranking of the domains those engines cite. Add include=web_baseline to see which AI-cited domains you do not yet rank on. Metered 2 credits per probe (one prompt x run x engine); use preset=quick|standard|deep for a flat budget. Appearance is detected deterministically via recognition tokens. Each answer is also judged for whether it recommends each brand, how favourably it treats it, and which brand it recommends first (recommended_rate, favourability_mean, primary_rate; null with a warning if that step is unavailable). Supply brand plus prompts (or a topic). The self-serve entry tier of Profound/Otterly/Peec.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 2-1605 credits a call — budget the 1605 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 2-1605 (metered): 2 credits per probe, where a probe is one prompt run once on one engine, so the charge is `2 x prompts x runs x engines`. On the defaults (both engines, 8 runs) a 5-prompt audit is 160 credits. `include=web_baseline` adds a flat 5. The 1,605 ceiling is the 20-prompt, 20-run, two-engine worst case with the baseline on - `preset=quick` holds far less, and the hold settles down to the probes that actually completed

**Parameters**

- `brand`: The brand whose appearance-% is measured (required). Matched against each answer plus its aliases.
- `competitors` *(optional)*: CSV of up to 5 competitors also measured for appearance-% from the same answers.
- `engines` *(optional)*: CSV subset of perplexity,grok (default both): the grounded-answer engines probed.
- `runs` *(optional)*: Reruns per (prompt, engine) to measure variance (1-20, default 8).
- `preset` *(optional)*: quick|standard|deep: sets runs and caps prompts for a flat probe budget.
- `include` *(optional)*: Set web_baseline to cross-join AI-cited domains against your web top domains.
- `brand_domains` *(optional)*: CSV of your own domains so the citation ranking can flag the ones you already rank on.
- `topic` / `prompts` — at least one required.
  - `topic`: A topic probed as a single prompt in v1 (one of prompts or topic is required). (one of: topic, prompts; at least one required)
  - `prompts`: The category prompts to probe, as a JSON array or a pipe-delimited list (1-20). One of prompts or topic is required. (one of: topic, prompts; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/ai-visibility?brand=<brand>&topic=<topic>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /crisis-postmortem — 35cr

Reconstructs a crisis window: content_analysis phrase-trends (volume curve) + anger-ordered search + reddit (sort=new) + hackernews (client-side date-filtered so stale relevance-ranked posts cannot corrupt the chronology) + search/everywhere (items_by_source cross-platform spread), merged into one chronologically-sorted event timeline with the first credible origin, the peak day, and the platform-by-platform propagation order. Pass include= (empty) to drop the LLM narrative and get the raw timeline. Origin is chosen only from natively-dated events (a lagged crawl time cannot establish who-said-it-first). Supply brand plus window_start; window_end defaults to today. Flat 35 credits; losing more than half the timeline sources refunds half.

**Parameters**

- `brand`: The brand or entity the crisis is about (required).
- `window_start` *(optional)*: Start of the crisis window (YYYY-MM-DD): the earliest point on the timeline. Optional; defaults to 30 days ago.
- `window_end` *(optional)*: End of the crisis window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.
- `crisis_terms` *(optional)*: Optional CSV of up to 5 terms (e.g. recall,defect) that scope the legs to the actual incident.
- `include` *(optional)*: narrative (default on) adds the grounded LLM propagation narrative; pass an empty value for the raw timeline only.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/crisis-postmortem?brand=<brand>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /crisis-radar — 15-45cr

Stage 1 computes a 7-day-rolling z-score on content_analysis daily phrase-trends (the breach gate, always 15 credits) and returns a calm|watch|alert|crisis status. On a breach with confirm=true, Stage 2 fans out to sentiment + search/everywhere (items_by_source real counts) + reddit (sort=new) + twitter/ai-search (citations, not the chatty answer) + a triage anger-ordered search, then grades severity (+30 credits, charged only when a breach actually fires). On an escalation every confirmation row is also judged (is it about this brand, and does it report an incident involving it): `severity.grade_about_brand`, `score_about_brand` and `reports_incident_with_brand` repeat the grade from the rows about the brand, next to the unchanged `grade`. A calm result or confirm=false costs only the 15cr baseline. The recurring alarm is delivered by wrapping this recipe in a monitor.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 15-45 credits a call — budget the 45 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 15-45 (metered): 15 credits for the baseline breach check. `confirm=true` escalates to the full 45-credit investigation. Run the baseline first and escalate only when it reports a breach: that is the whole point of the two-step shape

**Parameters**

- `brand`: The brand to watch.
- `sensitivity` *(optional)*: Z-score breach threshold (0.5-6, default 2.0). z>=sensitivity on volume or negative-share fires a breach.
- `confirm` *(optional)*: true -> on a breach, run the escalation legs and grade severity (+30 credits, charged only when a breach fires).
- `baseline_days` *(optional)*: Rolling-mean window for the z-score (3-30, default 7).
- `date_to` *(optional)*: The day being evaluated (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.
- `brand_description` *(optional)*: Optional one-line description of the brand, used to tell it apart from other things with the same name.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/crisis-radar?brand=<brand>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /devtool-pulse — 20cr

Fans out a GitHub repo/dossier, a Hacker News search+comment pull, a Reddit search+comment pull, and the dev-blog web echo (content_analysis), then folds them into a developer-brand health snapshot: release recency, open-issue load, the top feature request and top complaint, HN and Reddit attention, the web echo with its top domains, a deterministic pulse=strong|steady|cooling|quiet label, and a soft NLP sentiment label. No leg is individually critical: absence is signal; a strict-majority leg failure refunds half. Supply `repo=` (owner/repo or a github URL) to anchor the dossier; without it the server best-effort resolves one from the HN/web legs. `legs[]` reports each leg's status, cost, and latency.

**Parameters**

- `query`: The devtool name to sweep across Hacker News, Reddit, and the dev-blog index (e.g. Bun, Drizzle ORM, tRPC).
- `repo` *(optional)*: The repo to dossier: owner/repo or a github.com/{owner}/{repo} URL. Recommended for a precise dossier.
- `subreddit` *(optional)*: Optional scope for the Reddit leg (bare name, no r/): switches it to a subreddit search.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of dossier,hn,reddit,blogs (default all). Trims which legs run, not the flat price.
- `date_from` *(optional)*: Optional window start (YYYY-MM-DD) applied to the time-bounded legs.
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Optional window end (YYYY-MM-DD).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/devtool-pulse?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /leads — 50cr

Runs three exact-intent phrases ('alternative to X', 'X vs', 'switching from X') through content_analysis search in parallel, plus a Reddit (sort=new) and a Hacker News leg, then dedupes them into one feed. Since methodology leads/2 the ranking is judged: an AI classifier reads each candidate and answers five narrow questions (what the author is doing, whether the row is about the competitor product rather than a namesake, whether the author is a vendor, whether your offer would help them, how urgent the need is), and code combines those answers with recency and engagement into lead_score = (0.35 x P(asking, comparing or switching) + 0.20 x P(fits offer) + 0.15 x urgency/3 + 0.15 x recency + 0.15 x engagement) x P(about) x (1 - P(vendor)). Each lead carries intent { label, probabilities, about, seller, fits_offer, urgency, confidence } and lead_score; the label reads 'uncertain' when the classifier has no clear winner. Rows with P(about) below 0.3 (the snowflake on a Christmas jumper) are removed and their URLs listed in dropped_ids. The keyword intent_score and phrase_matched from leads-v1 are still on every row, and if the classifier is unavailable the feed falls back to that keyword order with _warnings: ['intent_unavailable'], intent: null and lead_score: null ('intent_partial' when only some rows could be judged). Conversation-level intent only: page-level matching, no author PII harvesting (web leads carry no handle by design, and no handle is sent to the classifier). Coverage spine is the three CA legs and does not depend on the classifier: <0.5 succeed → 50% refund; all five legs fail → full refund. Registers cleanly for a recurring-lead-feed monitor.

**Parameters**

- `competitor`: The competitor/product to mine alternative-seeking conversations for (≤80 chars).
- `product_category` *(optional)*: Optional disambiguator appended to the social queries to cut cross-domain noise (e.g. 'project management').
- `freshness` *(optional)*: Recency floor. Nd/Nw/Nm (e.g. 30d) or an ISO date. Default 30d.
- `include` *(optional)*: Set `comments` to attach top-thread Reddit comments to the top leads.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Max leads in the fused feed (1-100, default 50).
- `offer` *(optional)*: What you sell, in one or two plain sentences (max 300 chars). Used to judge whether each author would plausibly be helped by it (intent.fits_offer). Default: 'alternatives to {competitor}'.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/leads?competitor=<competitor>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /comment-leads — 0-243cr

Searches TikTok for `query`, decides which posts are worth opening, fetches the comments of those posts only, and returns the commenters who want to buy what you sell. Every searched post that reports comments is judged for whether people who want `offer` would plausibly comment under it; posts judged clearly off-offer are skipped, and the busiest of the rest (by reported comment count) are opened, up to `open`. Each fetched comment is then labelled for purchase intent (says they bought or want to buy, or asks for a link, a price or where to get it), for being a real question, for spam, and for whether `offer` would help its author; a comment is a lead when purchase intent is at least 0.5, spam below 0.5 and offer fit at least 0.5. Each lead carries the comment id and text, the commenter's public username and display name as the platform shows them, the post it came from and every probability. `posts_opened` gives per-post stats, `skipped_posts` lists every post not opened with its reason (`no_comments`, `no_url`, `below_gate`, `over_open_limit`) and its judgment, and `economics` reports posts searched and opened, comments fetched and judged, credits by leg, the credits held and refunded, an estimate of what opening every post would have cost at the same prices, and credits per lead. Measured on 15 real searches (5 Korean): with the default `open=12` it found 88% of the leads that opening every post found, at 0.96 credits a lead against 1.39. Posts that report no comments are never opened. If the post judgment is unavailable the busiest posts are opened instead (`_warnings: ['post_gate_unavailable']`); a comment that could not be labelled is never a lead and is not billed. `include=askers` adds comments that ask a question the offer would answer, as `kind: 'asker'`. Leads are labels for your own review: nothing is contacted.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 0-243 credits a call — budget the 243 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 0-243 (metered): Pay for what is opened: 1 credit a search page, 1 credit a comment page fetched and 1 credit for every started 25 comments labelled. The default request holds 37 and refunds what did not run; judging which posts to open is free

**Parameters**

- `query`: The keyword search to run (max 100 chars).
- `offer` *(optional)*: What you sell, in one or two plain sentences (max 300 chars). Used to judge which posts would draw your buyers and whether each commenter would be helped by it. Default: the `query` itself.
- `platform` *(optional)*: Platform to search. `tiktok` (default and, for now, only).
- `posts` *(optional)*: How many posts to search (1-90, default 30; 30 posts a search page).
- `open` *(optional)*: The most posts whose comments are fetched (1-20, default 12).
- `comments_per_post` *(optional)*: The most comments read from each opened post (1-200, default 50; 50 comments a page).
- `include` *(optional)*: Set `askers` to also return comments that ask a question the offer would answer, marked `kind: 'asker'`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/comment-leads?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /earned-media — 25cr

Fans out content_analysis news search, a Hacker News leg, and a fresh-web news leg in parallel, then dedupes and ranks them into one earned-media clip feed with computed top outlets, freshness labeling (content_analysis fetch_time lags the live web), and (when a `competitor` is supplied) a coverage gap. Each clipping also carries a judged `mention` label (is it about this brand, or a name collision), and `computed.clipping_count_about_brand`, `top_outlets_about_brand` and `coverage_gap_about_brand` repeat those numbers without the clippings judged to be about something else; the original numbers are unchanged. The content_analysis news leg is the coverage spine (losing it → 50% refund); Hacker News and the fresh-web leg are enrichment. `include=digest` adds an LLM narrative summary leg.

**Parameters**

- `brand`: The brand/company to map earned media for.
- `competitor` *(optional)*: Optional competitor for a share-of-coverage gap.
- `date_from` *(optional)*: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `min_domain_rank` *(optional)*: Drop clips from sites below this domain authority.
- `include` *(optional)*: Set `digest` to add an LLM narrative summary.
- `brand_description` *(optional)*: Optional one-line description of the brand, used to tell it apart from other things with the same name.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/earned-media?brand=<brand>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /truthsocial-pulse — 20cr

Fetches a Truth Social profile + recent posts, drills the top posts for full detail (the F13 post-detail path), and runs a content_analysis news echo for the handle, folded into a deterministic activity/sentiment pulse with stable keys + a methodology_version. The profile leg is critical (404 → full refund); posts/drill/news degrade. No Truth Social search exists upstream. This is handle-scoped.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: The Truth Social handle (no @).
- `drill` *(optional)*: How many top posts to drill for full detail (0 to skip).
- `posts` *(optional)*: How many recent posts to pull (window cap).
- `news_query` *(optional)*: Override the content_analysis news keyword (defaults to the handle/display name).
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of posts,news to trim which legs run.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Opaque pagination cursor for the posts leg.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/truthsocial-pulse?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /launch-echo — 20cr

Runs a Hacker News search, digs the top threads' comments, and pulls the dev-blog web echo (content_analysis), with an optional GitHub repo/dossier (explicit `repo=` or auto-resolved from the HN/web hits), folded into a launch-reception snapshot with computed attention + echo + a methodology_version. Comment legs are the coverage spine (<0.5 → 50% refund); a dead HN search → full refund.

**Parameters**

- `query`: The launch/product name to measure reception for.
- `repo` *(optional)*: Optional owner/repo or github URL to anchor the dossier.
- `threads` *(optional)*: How many top HN threads to dig comments for.
- `date_from` *(optional)*: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset toggling the comments/blogs/dossier legs.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/launch-echo?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /audience-overlap — 20cr

Samples each creator's recent videos and their commenters, then computes a deterministic audience-overlap: shared commenters, Jaccard index, a/b-only counts, and an honesty `confidence` label (commenters over-index super-fans: a lower bound, never full-audience truth). TikTok-only in v1 (YouTube/Instagram are a fast-follow); a non-tiktok `platform` is rejected. If either creator can't be fetched the overlap is undefined → full refund.

**Parameters**

- `handle_a`: First TikTok creator handle.
- `handle_b`: Second TikTok creator handle.
- `platform` *(optional)*: Platform (tiktok only in v1; default tiktok).
- `videos_per_creator` *(optional)*: Recent videos sampled per creator (1-10, default 5): caps the commenter pull.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Set `deep` to widen the shared-fan enrichment sample.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/audience-overlap?handle_a=<handle_a>&handle_b=<handle_b>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /reputation — 30cr

Resolves (a judgment picks which search result is the brand or app itself, reported in `entity_resolution`) and pulls reviews from Trustpilot, the Google Play + App Store listings, Google Business (and TripAdvisor when `place` is set), plus a content_analysis web-sentiment + rating-distribution read, then blends them into a renormalized weighted composite_score (company vs product axes) with per-source ratings (listed aggregate preferred over sample mean) and an LLM-themed pros/cons pass (counts + verbatim quotes recomputed in code). Coverage spine = the resolved sources (<0.5 → 50% refund; none → full refund); the theme pass degrades to empty without refund. Trustpilot review depth is clamped to 20.

**Parameters**

- `brand`: The brand/business/domain to assess.
- `sources` *(optional)*: CSV subset of trustpilot,google_play,app_store,google,tripadvisor,web (default the core set).
- `country` *(optional)*: Marketplace or locale, as a location name or numeric code (look one up with `GET /v1/content_analysis/locations`). Defaults to United States.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Reviews per source (Trustpilot clamped ≤20).
- `place` *(optional)*: Set to enable the place-based legs (Google Business + TripAdvisor).
- `axis` *(optional)*: Which reputation axis to headline: company, product, or both (default).
- `app_store_id` *(optional)*: App Store id to anchor that axis directly (skips resolver).
- `google_play_id` *(optional)*: Google Play id to anchor that axis directly (skips resolver).
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of `themes`, `response_rate`, `languages` (default: all three). Naming a subset TRIMS the report to those blocks; an unknown member or an empty value is a 400.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/reputation?brand=<brand>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /employer-brand — 30cr

Fans out a LinkedIn company + posts read (LinkedIn comments are excluded, no upstream endpoint), Reddit search + comment dig, content_analysis news + sentiment, a YouTube search, and Naver blog/cafe, then computes per-surface sentiment plus a posting-tone-vs-reality gap (the company's own LinkedIn voice vs the external chatter). Coverage spine = the requested surfaces (<0.5 → 50% refund; none → full refund); the LLM theme pass degrades without refund. Supply `linkedin_url` to include the LinkedIn axis (omitted silently otherwise).

**Parameters**

- `company`: The employer/company name.
- `linkedin_url` *(optional)*: The company's LinkedIn URL: enables the LinkedIn voice axis + the posting-vs-reality gap.
- `surfaces` *(optional)*: CSV subset of the surfaces to include.
- `phrases` *(optional)*: Optional extra Reddit search phrases.
- `timeframe` *(optional)*: Reddit timeframe window.
- `date_from` *(optional)*: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/employer-brand?company=<company>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
