### /audience-questions — 30cr

Searches Reddit and YouTube (and optionally the universal web search) for a topic, picks the titles and comments that ask a real question (a judgment per text, so Korean and other questions without a "?" count; `methodology.question_detection` reports how they were picked, with a punctuation heuristic as the fallback), and LLM-clusters them into labeled intent groups with verbatim quotes and per-question source counts (the model only labels/groups: counts and quotes are recomputed in code). The clustering degrades to one ungrouped cluster on LLM failure (no refund). Coverage spine = the per-source search legs (<0.5 → 50% refund; all dead → full refund). Great for content/SEO briefs and FAQ generation.

**Parameters**

- `topic`: The topic/keyword to mine audience questions for.
- `platforms` *(optional)*: CSV subset of reddit,youtube,web (default reddit,youtube).
- `max_questions` *(optional)*: Cap on questions returned.
- `threads_per_source` *(optional)*: How many top threads to dig per source.
- `timeframe` *(optional)*: Recency window.
- `include` *(optional)*: Set `web` to add the universal-search leg.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/audience-questions?topic=<topic>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /product-reviews — 30cr

Resolves a product on Amazon (ASIN) + Google Shopping (gid) + Trustpilot (when resolving by `query`, a judgment picks the result that is the product itself, not an accessory or reseller, and reports it in `entity_resolution`) and pulls each source's reviews, folded into a per-source rating summary (listed aggregate preferred over sample mean), a retailer matrix, and an LLM topic pass with per-topic rating impact (the model only assigns review ids: averages are recomputed in code). Anchor with `asin`/`gid` for precision (the gid is `product.ext.gid`, NOT the catalogid) or `query` to auto-resolve. Coverage spine = the resolved sources (<0.5 → 50% refund; none → full refund). Commerce legs take 20-60s.

**Parameters**

- `sources` *(optional)*: CSV subset of amazon,google_shopping,trustpilot (default all).
- `country` *(optional)*: Marketplace country, as a location name or numeric code (look one up with `GET /v1/content_analysis/locations`).
- `depth` *(optional)*: Reviews per source (Trustpilot clamped ≤20).
- `competitors` *(optional)*: Optional competitor products for a comparison (validated; deeper sweep is a fast-follow).
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of `topics`, `timeline`, `sellers`, `retailer_matrix`, `social_echo` (default: all five). Naming a subset TRIMS which blocks are computed; an unknown member or an empty value is a 400. `sellers` also needs `amazon` to be in scope.
- `query` / `asin` / `gid` — at least one required.
  - `query`: Product name to auto-resolve across marketplaces. (one of: query, asin, gid; at least one required)
  - `asin`: Amazon ASIN to anchor the Amazon axis directly. (one of: query, asin, gid; at least one required)
  - `gid`: Google product id (gid) to anchor the Google Shopping axis (NOT the catalogid). (one of: query, asin, gid; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/product-reviews?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /apps-lookup — 30cr

Resolves an app on both stores (by `title`, or directly via `google_play_id`/`app_store_id`), judges whether the two listings are the same app (so a Korean title matches its English listing and two same-named-but-different apps aren't conflated; the older title + developer string guard is the fallback, and `match_threshold` still applies it when you pass one), and folds the two listings into a cross-store comparison: per-store rating + install + price, the rating gap, and a match confidence. A clean no-match across stores is a valid (fully-charged) result; if neither store resolves the title → 404 + refund; both stores dead → full refund.

**Parameters**

- `stores` *(optional)*: CSV subset of google_play,app_store (default both).
- `country` *(optional)*: Store country.
- `language` *(optional)*: Store language.
- `match_threshold` *(optional)*: Title-similarity threshold for the cross-store match guard (0-1, default 0.6).
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of `merged`, `similar`, `developer` (default: all three). Naming a subset TRIMS which blocks are computed; an unknown member or an empty value is a 400.
- `title` / `google_play_id` / `app_store_id` — at least one required.
  - `title`: The app title to resolve across both stores. (one of: title, google_play_id, app_store_id; at least one required)
  - `google_play_id`: Google Play app id to anchor that store directly. (one of: title, google_play_id, app_store_id; at least one required)
  - `app_store_id`: App Store app id to anchor that store directly. (one of: title, google_play_id, app_store_id; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/apps-lookup?title=<title>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /org-radar — 6-51cr

Lists a GitHub org's repositories, picks the top N by stars (forks/archived filtered), and runs the repo/dossier composite on each in parallel, folded into an org-level rollup. Metered: 1cr to resolve the org + 5cr per repo dossiered; the unused per-repo credits are refunded down to the dossiers that actually succeeded. The org repo-list leg is critical (unknown org → 404 + full refund).

> ⚠️ **Metered: 6-51 credits a call — budget the 51 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 6-51 (metered): 1 credit for the org read plus 5 per repository expanded into a dossier. The default of 5 repos is 26 credits, a single repo is 6, and the 10-repo maximum is 51. Set `repos` to bound it before calling

**Parameters**

- `org`: The GitHub org login or a github.com/{org} URL.
- `repos` *(optional)*: How many top repos to dossier (1-10, default 5): drives the metered price.
- `sort` *(optional)*: Repo ranking: stars (default), updated, or pushed.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of `dossiers`, `rollup` (default: both). Naming a subset TRIMS which blocks are computed; an unknown member or an empty value is a 400. Dropping `dossiers` also drops the per-repo credit (`1 + 5 x repos` becomes `1`).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/org-radar?org=<org>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /creator-vet — 50-75cr

Pulls a creator's profile + recent posts + a commenter sample (TikTok / YouTube / Instagram) plus a news + Reddit + Hacker News controversy read, and computes authenticity signals in code: engagement rate, a low-quality-commenter share, posting cadence, and controversy inputs. Two judged blocks sit on top. `computed.brand_safety` reads the found items one by one and reports whether each is about this creator (namesakes are counted in `namesakes_excluded` and kept out), whether the creator is the one blamed rather than the victim, which kind of controversy it reports and how severe; every entry of `flagged_items` points at its source row (`source`, `index`, `url`) and `level` is the highest severity found (`none_found`, `minor`, `review`, `high`). `computed.comment_quality` reports `generic_share` (sampled comments that could sit under any video) and `repeated_share` (comments whose text appears more than once). The judgments are automated labels with probabilities, never generated text about a person, and every count and the level are computed in code; read the cited rows before acting on a flag. If the judged step is unavailable both blocks are `null`, `_warnings` says so, and everything else in the response is unchanged at the same price. `include=cross_platform` adds the universal cross-platform presence leg (+25cr, refunded if it fails). The core profile leg is critical (creator not found → full refund).

> ⚠️ **Metered: 50-75 credits a call — budget the 75 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 50-75 (metered): 50 credits for the standard vet. `include=cross_platform` raises it to 75 for the cross-platform identity check on top

**Parameters**

- `handle`: The creator handle to vet.
- `platform` *(optional)*: Primary platform (tiktok/youtube/instagram).
- `depth` *(optional)*: Set `deep` to widen the post + commenter sample.
- `include` *(optional)*: Set `cross_platform` to add the universal cross-platform presence leg (+25cr).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/creator-vet?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /adverse-screen — 25-75cr

Reads the recent public posts of a person's own profiles (one per platform: `linkedin`, `twitter`, `facebook`, `instagram`, `threads`, `tiktok`, each a handle or a profile URL) and asks, post by post, whether the author engages in, admits, threatens or promotes each category you screen for: `fraud_or_financial_crime`, `violence_or_threats`, `hate_or_harassment`, `drugs`, `sanctions_or_terror_links`, `sexual_misconduct`, `reputational_other` (default: all). A separate check keeps posts that report, quote, warn about or condemn what someone else did (news, a scam warning) from counting as the author's conduct, and a severity level (1 minor, 2 serious, 3 severe) is given for every flagged post. Every entry of `flags` cites its post (`platform`, `post_id`, `url`, `published_at`, an `excerpt`) with the probability for each requested category; `category_counts` counts flagged and uncertain posts per category; `requires_review` is true when any post is flagged. With `name` (and optionally `employer`, `city`), each profile is first checked against the named person: only profiles judged to be the person's own are screened, the rest are listed in `profiles` with the identity verdict and are not screened (`screen_unconfirmed=true` screens possible matches too, never a profile judged to be someone else). These are automated labels for a human reviewer, not a decision: there is no summary, verdict or score about the person, and political opinion, religion, health, sexuality and other personal characteristics are never screened. Public posts only; private accounts return nothing. `screen_complete` is false when a profile or a post could not be screened, and `_warnings` says why.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 25-75 credits a call — budget the 75 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 25-75 (metered): 25 credits for one profile, plus 10 for each further profile (4 profiles cost 55). Profiles that could not be screened are refunded their share, and a call that screened nothing keeps 5

**Parameters**

- `name` *(optional)*: The person's full name. When set, each profile is checked against it before screening.
- `employer` *(optional)*: Optional current employer, used only for the identity check.
- `city` *(optional)*: Optional city or country, used only for the identity check.
- `categories` *(optional)*: Comma-separated subset of fraud_or_financial_crime, violence_or_threats, hate_or_harassment, drugs, sanctions_or_terror_links, sexual_misconduct, reputational_other. Default: all. An unknown member is a 400.
- `since` *(optional)*: Only screen posts published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `limit` *(optional)*: Most recent posts screened per profile, 1 to 100 (default 50). One timeline page is read per profile.
- `screen_unconfirmed` *(optional)*: Set true to also screen profiles whose identity is possible or could not be judged. Profiles judged to be someone else are never screened.
- `linkedin` / `twitter` / `facebook` / `instagram` / `threads` / `tiktok` — at least one required.
  - `linkedin`: LinkedIn profile URL (linkedin.com/in/...) or the profile slug. (one of: linkedin, twitter, facebook, instagram, threads, tiktok; at least one required)
  - `twitter`: X (Twitter) handle or profile URL. (one of: linkedin, twitter, facebook, instagram, threads, tiktok; at least one required)
  - `facebook`: Facebook profile or page URL, or its username. (one of: linkedin, twitter, facebook, instagram, threads, tiktok; at least one required)
  - `instagram`: Instagram handle or profile URL. (one of: linkedin, twitter, facebook, instagram, threads, tiktok; at least one required)
  - `threads`: Threads handle or profile URL. (one of: linkedin, twitter, facebook, instagram, threads, tiktok; at least one required)
  - `tiktok`: TikTok handle or profile URL. (one of: linkedin, twitter, facebook, instagram, threads, tiktok; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/adverse-screen?linkedin=<linkedin>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /find-accounts — 2-17cr

Runs the existing account searches for `name` on each platform (`instagram/search/profiles`, `tiktok/search/users`, `twitter/search/users`, and `linkedin/search/people` for a person or `linkedin/search/companies` for a company), keeps the top `candidates` public accounts of each (private accounts are dropped), and ranks them. Each platform returns `candidates` (rank, handle, display name, profile URL, followers, verified flag, a bio excerpt and `choice_probability`, the judged probability that this account is the target's own) and one `match`: `handle` is the leading candidate, `level` is `same`, `possible` (connected but not shown to be the target's own, such as a fan or regional account), `different`, `uncertain` (the ranking was flat or the check was unsure), or `none` (none of the candidates is the target's own account, or the search found nothing), with `confidence` (the weaker of the ranking and the check), `basis` and `evidence` (`website_match`, `cross_link`, `bio_consistent`, `fan_or_parody`). The leading candidate is always checked a second time against the name and context you sent; a ranking alone is never a match. With `website`, an account that links to that site and is platform-verified is taken as the match without judging (`basis: exact_link`); an unverified account linking to it is judged like the rest. `employer` (person only) and `location` give the judgment context. These are automated labels for a human reviewer, not an identification: `automated_decision` is false and the response never states who runs an account. If the judgment is unavailable, candidates come back in search order with `match.level` null, `_warnings` says why, and the judging credits are refunded. LinkedIn is included by default for a company only, because its search costs 10 credits.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 2-17 credits a call — budget the 17 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 2-17 (metered): The searches at their own prices (1 credit each for Instagram, TikTok and X, 10 for LinkedIn) plus 1 credit per platform judged: 6 credits for a person by default, 17 for a company (LinkedIn included). A search that fails and a platform that could not be judged are refunded

**Parameters**

- `name`: The person's or the company's name, 2 to 120 characters.
- `type` *(optional)*: `person` (default) or `company`. Sets the default platforms and the LinkedIn search used.
- `platforms` *(optional)*: Comma-separated subset of linkedin, instagram, tiktok, twitter. Default: instagram, tiktok, twitter for a person; all four for a company. An unknown member is a 400.
- `employer` *(optional)*: Optional current employer of the person, used only as context for the judgment (type=person only).
- `location` *(optional)*: Optional city or country, used only as context for the judgment.
- `website` *(optional)*: Optional official website or domain (e.g. ogilvy.com). A platform-verified account linking to it is taken as the match without judging.
- `candidates` *(optional)*: Accounts judged per platform, 1 to 5 (default 5), taken from the top of each search.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/find-accounts?name=<name>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /mentions — 1-9cr

Pass handle (the @ is optional), or url (a link or a link prefix), or name on its own. platforms defaults to twitter, reddit, facebook. Opt in to instagram for posts that tag the handle, or web (url only) for a web page that contains the link. since is YYYY-MM-DD. include_self defaults to false and drops the account's own rows. Each kept row has match_kind reply, retweet, mention or tag. Unverified rows are dropped and counted in dropped_unverified. Url mode adds first_seen for the link. name is judged; a handle or a url is checked in code and is not judged. If that judgment is unavailable the rows are kept and warnings says why. Instagram comments on unknown posts cannot be searched, and Instagram caption mentions cannot. TikTok comments on unknown posts cannot be searched. Threads search is weak: measured 23/09/2026 it returned no row containing the handle, so Threads is not searched. Facebook post search returned no row containing the handle or the link on the same day, so Facebook is not searched. TikTok search for @handle returned no row containing that @, so TikTok is not searched. Bluesky has no search lane. LinkedIn is not covered. Private or deleted content is not covered. This is a first page of each search, not an index.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 1-9 credits a call — budget the 9 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 1-9 (metered): 1 credit for each X or Reddit page, 5 for an Instagram tag page, 1 for a web page. A default call holds 3. A page with no verified row is refunded. Facebook, Threads and TikTok are not searched.

**Parameters**

- `platforms` *(optional)*: Comma-separated subset of twitter, reddit, facebook, threads, instagram, tiktok, web. Default twitter, reddit, facebook. Instagram needs a handle. Web needs a url. Facebook, Threads and TikTok are accepted and not searched.
- `since` *(optional)*: Only keep rows published on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. On X it is also part of the search.
- `include_self` *(optional)*: When true, keep rows whose author is the handle. Default false.
- `handle` / `url` / `name` — at least one required.
  - `handle`: Account handle, with or without @. Checked in code. Not combined with name. (one of: handle, url, name; at least one required)
  - `url`: A link or a link prefix, such as example.com/news. Checked in code. Not combined with name. (one of: handle, url, name; at least one required)
  - `name`: A display name, 2 to 120 characters, passed on its own. Each row is judged. A failed judgment keeps the rows. (one of: handle, url, name; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/mentions?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /brief-check — 15cr

Pass a creator post URL and the brief: `points` (CSV of required talking points), optional `forbidden` (CSV of claims the creator must not make), and `require_disclosure=1` when a paid-partnership marker is required. The response lists each point with a coverage level (0 not mentioned, 1 passing mention, 2 explained, 3 explained with a demonstration) and a verbatim quote, any forbidden hits, whether a disclosure marker such as #ad or 광고 was present, and a verdict of pass or review. A post with no transcript is `no_transcript: true` and never passes a talking point on silence. These are labels for a reviewer, not an automatic action.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Absolute http(s) URL of one creator post or video.
- `points`: CSV of required talking points, for example 'Use the code SAVE20, Taste test on camera'.
- `forbidden` *(optional)*: CSV of claims the creator must not make, for example 'Cures disease'.
- `require_disclosure` *(optional)*: Set 1 when a paid-partnership disclosure such as #ad or 광고 is required to pass.
- `brand` *(optional)*: Optional brand name used when judging talking points about a product.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/brief-check?url=<url>&points=<points>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /format-lift — 4cr

Pass platform (youtube, tiktok, or instagram) and handle. The response files each recent post as a how-to, a story, a challenge, or none, then divides that post's views (or likes, when the platform publishes no views) by the median of the creator's other posts of the same type. Pinned posts are excluded. A post under 48 hours is marked too young and is not given a ratio. Fewer than eight comparable posts returns no baseline. A bucket under eight posts publishes the count and not a median. The price is provisional.

**Parameters**

- `platform`: youtube, tiktok, or instagram.
- `handle`: The creator's handle, without @.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/format-lift?platform=<platform>&handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /earliness — 25cr

Pass term, and an optional region. The response gives the earliest relevant post date on TikTok, X, Reddit, YouTube, and Instagram, the first non-zero Google Trends point, and whether an ad for the term is already in the TikTok or Meta library. Gaps are in days. A page whose oldest row is still within 30 days, and which did not reach the start of the index, is marked censored: first seen before that date, not a first-seen date. A different subject that shares the words is not counted. Ads that are not about the term do not make it late. The price is provisional.

**Parameters**

- `term`: The phrase, sound title, hashtag, or trend name to date.
- `region` *(optional)*: Optional country code passed to the lanes that accept one, such as US.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/earliness?term=<term>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /trend-board — 30cr

Pass country_code (an ISO code Google Trends covers, such as DE). The board is computed live for this call and nothing is stored between calls, so there is no history and no days parameter: repeat calls within 15 minutes are served from cache. `breakout_posts` are videos on TikTok's local feed for that country, registered there, whose views are at least 3 times the median of the author's own recent posts (pinned posts and posts under 48 hours are left out, at least 8 posts are compared, and rows without enough posts are counted, not shown). `rising_sounds` are the sounds used most on that feed, with how many of each sound's first page of videos are from the last 3 days and whether it is a returning or new sound. `rising_hashtags` are TikTok's own hashtag board for the country, with growth from its daily popularity curve and the first day in the window it was non-zero. `rising_searches` are Google Trends Trending Now, where Google's own start time is the first-seen date. `sources` and `unavailable` say which parts answered. TikTok's hashtag board covers 27 markets; elsewhere that section is empty and says why. No language model is used. Music charts and Pinterest Trends are not included yet. The price is provisional.

**Parameters**

- `country_code`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as DE, US or KR. Any country Google Trends Trending Now covers.
- `period` *(optional)*: 7 (default) or 30. The window of TikTok's hashtag board. Google Trending Now is always read over its longest window, 7 days.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Rows per section, 1 to 10. Default 10.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/trend-board?country_code=<country_code>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /audience-language — 2-26cr

Pass platform (tiktok, instagram or youtube) and handle. The response is the language mix of comments on the creator's recent posts: Hangul, Kana, Thai and Han are read from the script, and Latin-script comments are classified with a closed list that includes cannot_tell. Each language is a share with n, how many were counted, how many were abstained, a 90% interval, and up to three verbatim comments. A share whose interval is wider than 0.25 has no headline number. On TikTok the follower sample from the audience call and the location field on one follower page sit beside that mix, each with its own n. The result is a language, never a country. A divergence flag is set only when both sides have at least 200 rows and the main language does not match the main follower country. posts is 1 to 5 and defaults to 5.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 2-26 credits a call — budget the 26 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 2-26 (metered): Floor 2 credits (one YouTube post: the channel list plus one comment page). Each further comment page is 1 credit, or 5 on Instagram, up to 5 posts. TikTok also opens the audience sample (5) and one follower page (1). Unopened pages are refunded. Five Instagram posts is 26 credits.

**Parameters**

- `platform`: tiktok, instagram or youtube.
- `handle`: Creator handle, with or without @.
- `posts` *(optional)*: How many recent posts to open comments for. 1 to 5. Default 5.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/audience-language?platform=<platform>&handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /korea-gap — 15-40cr

Fans the Korean Naver corpora (news/blog/cafe/kin/shop/web) against the global conversation (the universal /search/everywhere leg) and computes a directional presence gap: which surface over-indexes the topic, a per-channel Korean map, and a translated quote sample (KR→EN, soft LLM). Metered 40cr full; `include` without `social` drops the everywhere leg for the 15cr web-only variant. Korean volume is a directional per-surface presence index (item-count-bounded), not absolute counts.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 15-40 credits a call — budget the 40 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 15-40 (metered): 15 credits for the web-only read. The default `include` carries the social leg, which makes the call 40; pass an `include` without `social` to stay at 15

**Parameters**

- `query`: The brand/topic to compare across the global and Korean conversations.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of `social` (the cross-platform everywhere leg) and `quotes` (the LLM translation pass), default both. An unknown member is a 400. Note the price runs the OTHER way from `video-intel` and `creator-vet`: DROPPING `social` moves the call from 40 credits to the 15-credit web-only variant.
- `date_from` *(optional)*: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `display` *(optional)*: Naver results per corpus.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/korea-gap?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /share-of-voice — 20-200cr

Per brand, fans out to content_analysis summary/phrase-trends/sentiment plus /search/everywhere (consuming the real per-platform items_by_source counts, not the capped fused list), then computes a published-formula SOV (web + social, equal-weighted by default), optional true-share-of-category (numeric `category_code`), and ESOV (`market_shares`, Binet/Field: a planning signal, not a growth guarantee). The web share is divided from the windowed phrase-trends sum over `date_from`..`date_to`, never from the upstream's all-time `total_count`, which is censored at 4,000,000 and would tie any two brands above that cap at exactly 50/50; the all-time figure still rides along per brand as `web_mentions_all_time` with a `web_mentions_all_time_censored` flag. One axis is chosen for the whole table and named in `methodology.web_axis`, so a brand whose timeline is unavailable can never be compared against a rival's on a different footing; if no brand's timeline is available the table falls back to the all-time totals and `_warnings` states that your window was not applied, and if those totals are censored it returns no web share at all instead of a fabricated tie. Every measured brand is scored on the SAME evidence basis: if one brand's social leg returns nothing, the whole table drops to the axes every brand has, `methodology.basis` names it, and `_warnings` says which brand caused it, so the column is always a real share rather than a mix of formulas. `methodology` ships the weights, the formula, the axis and the denominators, so you can recompute any share by hand from the same payload. With the social leg on, each brand's highest-engagement social rows (up to `methodology.about_brand.max_rows_per_brand`) are also judged for whether they are about that brand at all, and a second set of numbers is published next to the first, never in place of it: `engagement_sum_about_brand`, `social_sov_pct_about_brand` and `sov_pct_about_brand` leave out the rows under `methodology.about_brand.about_brand_at_or_above`, and `per_brand[].about_brand` lists the excluded row ids, their engagement, and the negative mentions by aspect. The web axis is an index count and is not cleaned. If any brand's rows could not be judged the cleaned numbers are null for the whole table and `_warnings` says `about_brand_unavailable`. The price is the same either way. Metered at 40cr/brand (20 web-only); a brand whose social search half-failed is automatically cheaper, with the reason legible in `legs[]` + per-brand `coverage`.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 20-200 credits a call — budget the 200 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 20-200 (metered): 40 credits per brand with the social leg, which is the default, or 20 per brand for the web-only read. Up to 5 brands per call, so the 200-credit ceiling is 5 brands with social and dropping `social` from `include` halves it. Price the call as `brands x per-brand` before you send it - this is the most expensive composite on the API

**Parameters**

- `brands`: 2-5 competitor brand names (CSV).
- `category_code` *(optional)*: Numeric category-taxonomy code for true-share-of-category (look one up with `GET /v1/content_analysis/categories`).
- `market_shares` *(optional)*: JSON map of real market share per brand (fraction or %), e.g. {"notion":0.4,"coda":0.25,"airtable":0.35}, to compute ESOV.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV toggles (default `emotions,social`). Drop `social` for the cheaper web-only variant; drop `emotions` to skip the sentiment leg. The emotion overlay is third-party NLP passed through unmodified and is not scoped to your date window; `methodology.sentiment_provenance` states that on every response that carries it.
- `page_type` *(optional)*: Optional surface filter forwarded to the content_analysis legs.
- `date_from` *(optional)*: Window start (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 90 days ago.
- `date_to` *(optional)*: Window end (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.
- `brand_descriptions` *(optional)*: Optional JSON map of a one-line description per brand, e.g. {"notion":"the workspace app"}, used to tell a brand apart from its namesakes.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/share-of-voice?brands=<brands>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /review-integrity — 30cr

Computes a documented, reproducible integrity grade for a product or brand by comparing ratings across Amazon, Google Shopping, Trustpilot, and the open web: cross-source rating divergence (Welch t-test), web-distribution bimodality (Sarle's coefficient), unsolicited-forum tone contrast, and spam-domain clustering. The grade uses no AI: every number is a published formula (`methodology_version`). When you pass `query`, a judgment picks which search result is the product itself and not an accessory or reseller (`entity_resolution`, with `resolved_by` and a confidence per source); it falls back to the first result, and a source with no matching listing is dropped with an `entity_not_found:<source>` warning. Returns the grade, per-signal evidence, per-source ratings, the divergence pair, and the raw sampled reviews. Reviewer-history tests are flagged `unavailable` (no upstream reviewer-profile source). Anchor on `asin`/`gid` for precision or `query` to auto-resolve. Commerce data takes 20-60s.

**Parameters**

- `sources` *(optional)*: CSV subset of amazon,google_shopping,trustpilot,web,forums (default all).
- `country` *(optional)*: Marketplace country, as a location name or numeric code (look one up with `GET /v1/content_analysis/locations`). Defaults to United States.
- `query` / `asin` / `gid` — at least one required.
  - `query`: Product or brand name to evaluate. (one of: query, asin, gid; at least one required)
  - `asin`: Amazon ASIN to anchor the Amazon axis directly (skips product-search). (one of: query, asin, gid; at least one required)
  - `gid`: Google product id (gid) to anchor the Google Shopping axis (NOT the catalogid product.id). (one of: query, asin, gid; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/review-integrity?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /answers — 15cr

Fans your question to multiple AI engines in parallel and keeps each answer verbatim, merges + dedupes their citations by normalized URL (with a `cited_by` list), and computes where they agree and disagree: a pairwise `agreement_matrix` + `disputed_claims` (the one labeled LLM step: degrades to null on failure) plus a deterministic `citation_overlap` (Jaccard, hand-verifiable). The second-opinion API for agents: one question, one bounded-cost call. Streams each engine's answer as it settles (SSE). `include=polymarket` adds probabilistic-market grounding. 15cr flat; a strict-majority engine failure refunds half (the raw answers are always the floor value).

**Parameters**

- `query`: The question, forwarded verbatim to every engine.
- `engines` *(optional)*: CSV subset of perplexity,grok,tavily (default all three).
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV of optional grounding legs: `polymarket` adds market probabilities (trimmed).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/answers?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /video-intel — 5-15cr

Fans out the video detail, comments, an optional transcript (10cr, never charged when the video has none), and ≤3 commenter profiles, folding them into one unified payload. Every leg joins on the same video `url`. Sync by default; streams Server-Sent Events when `include=transcript` (the transcript leg can take 20s+). `legs[]` reports each fired leg's status, cost, and latency; `coverage` + `partial_failure` flag any degraded leg. Commenter profiles ship for TikTok + Instagram in v1.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 5-15 credits a call — budget the 15 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 5-15 (metered): 5 credits for the video detail, stats and comments. `include=transcript` adds 10, which is exactly what the standalone transcript endpoint charges, so the bundle never costs more than running the two calls yourself

**Parameters**

- `url`: Absolute http(s) URL of a YouTube, TikTok, Rumble, or Instagram video.
- `comments` *(optional)*: How many top comments to fetch (0-50, default 20). `0` skips the comments leg.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV of optional costed legs: `transcript` (adds the dedicated transcript leg, +10cr, refunded when null) and/or `commenter_profiles` (≤3 commenter mini-profiles, TikTok/Instagram in v1).
- `app_demand` *(optional)*: Optional. 1 reads the caption first, then the comments, and returns data.app_demand: late when the caption already names an app, otherwise the count of comments that want an app they do not have, the count that name one, and that ratio. The ratio is withheld unless the comments support it. A low-confidence comment is not counted. No extra credits.
- `claim` *(optional)*: Optional sentence. When set, data.sense_check says whether the comments support it, contradict it, or say nothing. A confidence under the cut, or one high-confidence contradiction, withholds the sentence. No extra credits.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/video-intel?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /voice — 5cr

Fetches a handle's recent posts from four microblogs in parallel, time-merges them into one chronological feed, and computes platform presence, a cross-post rate, and a per-platform tone label (a soft LLM heuristic that degrades to absent on failure). Microblogs the handle isn't on return empty arrays with `platform_presence:false`: the absence map is the product. Flat 5cr; all-miss → full refund. The `legs[]` block reports each leg's status, cost, and latency. X pages: pass a prior `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. v1 is list-level (no per-post detail drill).

**Parameters**

- `handle`: The handle to look up across all four microblogs (a single leading @ is stripped).
- `platforms` *(optional)*: CSV subset of twitter,threads,bluesky,truthsocial (default all four).
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Opaque composite cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`. X/Twitter pages; Truth Social pages on `next_max_id`; a mangled token is a 400 at 0 credits.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of posts_by_platform,merged_timeline,computed to trim the payload (posts_by_platform is always returned).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/voice?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /app-reviews — 10-15cr

One call returns a topic-clustered, sentiment-classified review report across Google Play and the App Store: per-store rating summary (listed aggregate), topic clusters, a pooled daily sentiment timeline, extracted feature requests, and developer-response rate, plus every raw review on the shared canonical Review shape. Resolve by store app_id (com.spotify.music / 324684580) or by `query` to auto-resolve the top app on each requested store. Sync by default; streams Server-Sent Events when the client sends `Accept: text/event-stream` (the review legs plus clustering run ~30s). Single-store calls are 10 credits; both stores 15.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 10-15 credits a call — budget the 15 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 10-15 (metered): 10 credits for one store, 15 for both. A bare `query` resolves both stores and costs 15; naming a single store in `stores`, or passing only one of `google_play_id` / `app_store_id`, costs 10

**Parameters**

- `country` *(optional)*: Storefront country, as a location name or numeric code (look one up with `GET /v1/app_store/locations` or `GET /v1/google_play/locations`). Defaults to United States.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language code (e.g. en).
- `depth` *(optional)*: Reviews per store (default 150 Google / 50 Apple, max 600). The App Store returns ~50 at depth 40.
- `stores` *(optional)*: CSV subset of google_play,app_store. Defaults to whichever ids/query resolve.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV of topics,sentiment_timeline,feature_requests,responses (default all). Omitting topics+feature_requests skips the LLM step.
- `google_play_id` / `app_store_id` / `query` — at least one required.
  - `google_play_id`: Google Play package name (e.g. com.spotify.music). (one of: google_play_id, app_store_id, query; at least one required)
  - `app_store_id`: App Store numeric app id (e.g. 324684580). (one of: google_play_id, app_store_id, query; at least one required)
  - `query`: App name to auto-resolve the top hit on each requested store (when no id is given). (one of: google_play_id, app_store_id, query; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/app-reviews?google_play_id=<google_play_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /creator-card — 5-8cr

Looks up a single handle across multiple platforms in parallel and returns one unified author card per platform (followers, verified flag, bio, ids) with null for the platforms the handle isn't found on, plus combined follower totals and an any-verified flag. The default set is TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and Twitter; Threads, Bluesky, and Truth Social can be added via `platforms`. A handle existing on only some platforms is a successful, complete answer (the nulls are the product); only an all-platform miss refunds. Flat 5 credits for up to 4 platforms, +1 credit per extra platform. `legs[]` reports each platform leg's status, cost, and latency. A handle existing on a platform does not mean it is the same creator there: send `verify=true` to get an `identity` verdict per platform (same, possible, different) with the evidence, at the same price.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 5-8 credits a call — budget the 8 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 5-8 (metered): 5 credits covering any 4 platforms, plus 1 credit per platform beyond 4. The default selection is 4 platforms, so the 7-platform maximum is 8 credits

**Parameters**

- `handle`: The handle to look up across every requested platform (a single leading @ is stripped).
- `platforms` *(optional)*: CSV subset of tiktok,instagram,youtube,twitter,threads,bluesky,truthsocial (default the first four). Unknown platforms are ignored.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of cards,totals to trim the payload (cards is always returned).
- `verify` *(optional)*: Send `true` to add an `identity` block that says whether each found profile is the same person or organisation as the anchor profile, not only that the handle exists there. Each platform gets a verdict with `level` (`same`, `possible`, `different`, or `uncertain` when the answer is not confident), a `score`, a `confidence` and the `evidence` behind it (`cross_link`, `bio_consistent`, `fan_or_parody`, `website_match`). A `null` verdict means that profile was not judged, not that it is different. `identity.verified_on` lists the anchor plus every `same` platform. Public profile text only, no image comparison. Same price; adds well under a second.
- `anchor` *(optional)*: With `verify=true`, the platform whose profile you already trust; every other found profile is compared against it. Omit it and the anchor is the platform-verified profile with the largest audience. If the chosen platform has no card in the response the anchor is picked automatically and `_warnings` says so.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/creator-card?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /handle-audit — 5-8cr

Decide whether to pull a handle before paying for a full collection. Score model 2.0.0 returns nullable top-level and per-platform scores, explicit evidence and component coverage, surface estimates, and `legs[]` diagnostics. Unknown numeric values are `null`, not zero. Output is deterministic only for the same (`score_version`, `evidence_fingerprint`) and returned evidence; a later live collection may produce different evidence and a different score. Stale-if-error evidence is eligible for at most 24 hours, and future-dated evidence more than 300 seconds ahead is rejected. 5 credits for any selection of up to 4 supported platforms; +1 credit per selected platform beyond 4. Every successful HTTP 200 receives the full request-shaped charge with no partial refund. A non-200 execution failure receives a full refund when every requested platform is a definitive miss or cannot return usable profile evidence. Scores are advisory estimates from public evidence, not calibrated probabilities.

Supported platforms are tiktok, instagram, youtube, twitter, threads, bluesky, truthsocial. Default platforms are tiktok, instagram, youtube, twitter. Optional platforms are threads, bluesky, truthsocial. Reddit is deferred and not supported.

Any unknown platform rejects the whole request with HTTP 400 before billing.

The identity may be a bare handle or canonical supported profile URL. A YouTube channel ID is YouTube-only: omit `platforms` to audit YouTube or set `platforms=youtube`; other canonical profile URLs do not narrow the default fanout.

YouTube sampled-post collection sends includeExtras=true.

Profile evidence states are live, stale, not_found, and unavailable. Posts evidence states are sampled, observed_empty, not_supported, not_found, and unavailable. Stale platforms are also listed in `stale_platforms`. Unknown numeric values are null, not zero, and decision-grade post evidence is required for scoring.

When a platform's profile evidence is not_found, its `not_found_reason` says why: account_gone (removed, renamed, or never existed), account_private (the account exists but is not publicly readable), or handle_unresolved (no source stated a cause), the same vocabulary the profile endpoints publish as `error.details.reason`. `not_found_reason` is null on every platform whose profile was found or not observed. It is reported only and never changes the score or verdict.

`observed_empty` is decision-grade evidence of an empty posting history; `days_since_last_post`, `media_fraction`, `avg_text_length`, and the `content_richness` score stay null because no posts were observed.

Explicitly empty text is observed as length 0 and explicitly empty media is observed as false; unknown text or media stays null. Content-richness uses known-only inputs and re-normalizes across the known inputs instead of treating unknowns as zero.

`legs[]` is emitted in stable plan order. A genuinely pending leg abandoned at the global deadline is synthesized as 504 / UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT / 0 credits; an early rejected dispatch is 502 / UPSTREAM_ERROR / 0 credits, including when compatible stale evidence recovers the response. A terminal profile failure emits no speculative posts leg.

Scores are reproducible only when `score_version` and `evidence_fingerprint` are unchanged; score and evidence fields can be null when decision-grade evidence is unavailable.

Collection has a 6.4-second default budget, a 6.5-second hard cap, and a 7-second public API target. These are configured targets, not measured v2 performance.

Process-local monotonic last-known-good ordering prevents older writers within one process; global atomic CAS remains future work.

With `relevant_to`, up to 25 of the posts already sampled (live evidence only, taken in turn across platforms) are judged against your subject by the same published relevance rule as `relevance=filter`. `domain_relevance.score` is the share kept, 0 to 100, with the posts judged listed in `judged_posts`.

`score_with_domain_relevance` is 0.7 x `score` + 0.3 x `domain_relevance.score`, and `verdict_with_domain_relevance` applies the same thresholds to it. `score`, `verdict`, the five base components, their weights and `evidence_fingerprint` never read the subject.

`domain_relevance` is null with a `_warnings` entry when fewer than 3 posts could be judged (`domain_relevance_insufficient_sample`) or the judging step did not answer (`domain_relevance_unavailable`). It is a judged estimate to review, not a measurement. Without `relevant_to` none of these fields is present.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 5-8 credits a call — budget the 8 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 5-8 (metered): 5 credits for any selection of up to 4 supported platforms; +1 credit per selected platform beyond 4

**Parameters**

- `handle`: The identity to audit. Accepts a bare handle, a leading @, a supported profile URL, or a YouTube channel ID. A YouTube channel ID is YouTube-only: omit `platforms` or set `platforms=youtube`.
- `platforms` *(optional)*: CSV subset of tiktok,instagram,youtube,twitter,threads,bluesky,truthsocial (default: tiktok,instagram,youtube,twitter). Names are case-insensitive and deduplicated. Unknown platforms are rejected. At most 8 CSV members before deduplication.
- `sample` *(optional)*: Integer from 1 to 25: recent posts sampled per found platform for engagement and activity metrics (default 10).
- `relevant_to` *(optional)*: Optional. Your subject in up to 200 characters, for example relevant_to=video games. Name ONE subject: `A and B` is read as posts about both. Adds domain_relevance (the share of sampled posts about it) and score_with_domain_relevance next to the unchanged score. No extra charge.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/handle-audit?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### **POST** /post-stats — 1-500cr

Bulk stats refresh for verification loops (clipper payouts). POST a JSON body with a `urls` array (1-100 mixed-platform post links); returns one row per URL: platform, status (ok / not_found / error / unsupported), the unified engagement block (views/likes/comments/shares/saves/reposts), and a server `fetched_at` timestamp: in input order. An Instagram row carries the same counts as `GET /v1/instagram/post/stats`, including the save count and the repost count when Instagram's response includes them (for a save count on every reel, use that endpoint with include=saves), and accepts every Instagram permalink form, including `instagram.com/<handle>/p/<code>/` as returned by `/v1/instagram/profile/posts`. Per-URL isolation: one dead link never fails the batch. Metered per successful URL at that URL's platform rate: 1 credit on most platforms, 2 credits for an Instagram post (5 on the single Instagram post stats endpoint) and 5 for LinkedIn post stats; dead, errored, and unsupported URLs are refunded, so you pay exactly for the counts you got. Never cached (every call reads the live count). Optionally streams Server-Sent Events when the client sends `Accept: text/event-stream`.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 1-500 credits a call — budget the 500 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 1-500 (metered): 1 credit per successful URL on most platforms, 2 on Instagram and 5 on LinkedIn, charged at each URL's own platform rate. Up to 100 URLs per call: the call holds the summed worst case up front (a 100-URL Instagram batch holds 200) and refunds every dead, errored and unsupported URL, so you pay for exactly the rows that returned counts

**Parameters**

- `urls` *(body)*: 
- `include` *(body, optional)*: 

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/post-stats" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls": "<urls>"}'
```

### **POST** /comment-lookup — 2-100cr

Batch version of the single-comment lookup, built for recurring brand-comment tracking. Pass up to 25 items, each either `{ comment_url }` or `{ platform, post_url, comment_id }` (plus optional `parent_comment_id`, `position_hint`, `deep_scan`). Every item resolves independently (one bad item never fails the batch) and returns a `status` of `found`, `not_found`, `error`, or `deferred`. Billing is per item (TikTok 2 credits, Instagram 5 credits; deep_scan raises it); only `found` items are charged, everything else is refunded, and the whole batch holds at most 100 credits. Store each returned `lookup.position_hint` and pass it back on the next run so a daily refresh of your tracked comments costs ~1-2 credits per item. Returns sync JSON, or a typed SSE stream (`Accept: text/event-stream`) that emits each item as it settles. Items not started within the 45-second budget come back `deferred` (refunded): just re-request them.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 2-100 credits a call — budget the 100 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 2-100 (metered): 2 credits per found TikTok item and 5 per found Instagram item, raised by `deep_scan`. Up to 25 items per call: the whole batch holds at most 100 credits up front and refunds every not_found, errored and deferred item

**Parameters**

- `items` *(body)*: 

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/comment-lookup" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items": "<items>"}'
```

### **POST** /profiles — 1-250cr

Batch profile lookup for handle vetting. POST a JSON body with an `items` array of 1-50 `{ platform, handle, custom_id? }` objects (handle accepts an @handle, a bare handle, or a pasted profile URL); returns one row per item: the canonical Author object (same shape as the single GET profile endpoint), a `status` of ok / not_found / unsupported / error / deferred, the caller's `custom_id` echoed, and the credits that row cost: in input order. Per-item isolation: one dead or private handle never fails the batch. Billing is per item at each platform's own credit tier (most platforms 1 credit; LinkedIn 5); only successful rows are charged, everything else is refunded. Supported platforms: instagram, tiktok, youtube, twitter, threads, twitch, snapchat, truthsocial, bluesky, kwai, linkedin, facebook. Never cached. Optionally streams Server-Sent Events when the client sends `Accept: text/event-stream`. Send `include: "posts"` (up to 25 items) to add each handle's first page of posts beside its profile: every ok row gains a `posts` block with the same post rows, `next_cursor` and `has_more` as that handle's own post list endpoint (`endpoint` names it: instagram profile/posts, tiktok profile/videos, youtube channel/videos, twitter user/tweets, threads user/posts, facebook profile/posts; other platforms answer `posts.status: "unsupported"`). `since` on the body and `stop_at_id` on an item stop each page at a date or at a post you already hold, as on those endpoints, and `posts.stopped_at` says which. The profile in `data` is unchanged.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 1-250 credits a call — budget the 250 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 1-250 (metered): 1 credit per successful row on most platforms and 5 on LinkedIn, charged at each handle's own platform tier. Up to 50 items per call: the call holds the summed worst case up front and refunds every not_found, unsupported, errored and deferred row. With include: "posts" (up to 25 items) a row also costs its post list page, 1 credit, charged only when that page came back with posts

**Parameters**

- `items` *(body)*: 
- `include` *(body, optional)*: 
- `since` *(body, optional)*: 

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/profiles" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items": "<items>"}'
```

### **POST** /jobs — no ceiling

Runs a batch too large for one call in the background. POST a JSON body `{ "endpoint": "prism/profiles" | "prism/post-stats", "items": [...] }` with 1 to 5,000 items in the item shape that endpoint takes (`{ platform, handle, custom_id?, stop_at_id? }` or `{ url, custom_id? }`). The job is split into chunks of 50 (25 with include: "posts") and each chunk runs exactly as a call to that endpoint would: same sources, same rows, same per-row price. The response is 202 with `job_id`; read `GET /v1/prism/jobs/{job_id}` for status and results. Every item is validated before anything is held, and a bad item is a 400 that names its position. Add `webhook: { url }` (public https) to be told when the job completes: the 202 returns `webhook.secret` once, and each delivery is signed in the `x-socialcrawl-signature` header as `t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">`. The webhook carries the summary and a results URL, not the rows. An `Idempotency-Key` header returns the existing job instead of a second one.

> ⚠️ **No ceiling can be computed for this call — the credit guard asks before every one.** Vendor label: The same price per row as the batch endpoint the job runs: prism/profiles (1 credit per profile on most platforms, 5 on LinkedIn, plus 1 per posts page with include: "posts") or prism/post-stats (its per-URL price). The call holds the whole job's worst case up front, answered in credits_used on the 202, and refunds every row that is not ok when the job completes. Reading the job is free.

**Parameters**

- `endpoint` *(body)*: 
- `items` *(body)*: 
- `include` *(body, optional)*: 
- `since` *(body, optional)*: 
- `webhook` *(body, optional)*: 

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/jobs" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"endpoint": "<endpoint>", "items": "<items>"}'
```

### /jobs — 0cr

Lists the jobs submitted with this API key to POST /v1/prism/jobs, newest first, 20 per page: status, item and chunk counts, credits held and charged, and the summary once complete. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. Free.

**Parameters**

- `cursor` *(optional)*: The previous response's next_cursor.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/jobs" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /jobs/{job_id} — 0cr

Returns one job from POST /v1/prism/jobs: `status` (queued, running, completed or failed), `chunks_done` of `chunk_count`, credits held and charged, the 9-field `summary` once complete, and `results`: the rows of up to five finished chunks, each row exactly as the batch endpoint returns it plus `index`, its position in the submitted items. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next rows; it is null at the end and while the next chunk is still running, and `results_complete` is true once every row has been read. A job whose every row failed upstream is `failed` and charged nothing. Rows the chunk's time limit did not reach come back `deferred` at 0 credits: submit them again. Results are kept for 7 days. Free.

**Parameters**

- `job_id`: The job id (bj_…) returned by POST /v1/prism/jobs as data.job_id.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: The previous response's next_cursor (a chunk position).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/jobs/<job_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /investigate — no ceiling

Given `goal`, each step picks the next read-only operation (search TikTok, search Instagram, open a profile found earlier, read a post's comments, or finish) from what earlier steps returned. Code owns the catalogue, removes operations already tried, caps steps and credits, and builds candidate ids from actual responses: the walker never invents a handle or URL. The response is `{ trail, results, stopped_because, credits_used }`. `stopped_because` is `goal_met`, `budget`, `step_limit` or `blocked`. Finish is refused until the walk has enough to answer `goal`. Partial trails are returned when the cap is hit, so you can restart from a step. Leads and labels on gathered rows are signals for your own review.

> ⚠️ **No ceiling can be computed for this call — the credit guard asks before every one.** Vendor label: Holds `budget` credits (default 40, max 200) up front and refunds what the walk does not spend. Each underlying page is charged at its own price. Deciding the next step is free.

**Parameters**

- `goal`: What you want to find, in one or two sentences (max 500 chars).
- `budget` *(optional)*: Credits held up front for the walk (1-200, default 40). Unused credits are refunded.
- `max_steps` *(optional)*: Most steps the walk may take (1-12, default 8).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/investigate?goal=<goal>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Prism endpoint

⚠️ **This platform holds the most expensive calls in the API.** Costs run from 0 to 50 credits
with no tier ladder — the label tells you nothing, so read the number every time. Anything at
25cr or above is a one-shot report, not a data pull: decide the question before you spend, and
confirm with the user first.

### Free and near-free — reach for these constantly

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Any social/commerce URL → the right detail endpoint | `/lookup` | **1–5** |
| Every comment on a post, replies nested, paged to completion | `/comments` | 1 |
| Up to 100 post URLs → current engagement | `POST /post-stats` | 1 **per URL** |
| Up to 50 (platform, handle) pairs → one Author each | `POST /profiles` | 1 **per item** |
| Re-check up to 25 known comments | `POST /comment-lookup` | 2 **per item** |
| AI share-of-voice / GEO monitoring | `/ai-visibility` | 2 |
| One handle's unified cards across platforms | `/creator-card` | 5 |
| One video → detail + stats + comments | `/video-intel` | 5 |
| One person's posts across X/Threads/Bluesky/Truth Social | `/voice` | 5 |
| **Should I even pull this handle?** | `/handle-audit` | 5 |

> ### ⚠️ The three `POST` batch endpoints are metered PER ROW, not per call
> This is the most expensive misreading available in the API, and the plugin shipped it wrong
> until 08.08.26. The credit figure is the price of **one row**, not of the request:
>
> | Endpoint | Per row | Worst case |
> |----------|---------|-----------|
> | `POST /post-stats` | 1cr most platforms, **2cr Instagram**, **5cr LinkedIn** | 100 IG URLs = **200cr** |
> | `POST /profiles` | 1cr most, **5cr LinkedIn** | 50 LinkedIn handles = **250cr** |
> | `POST /comment-lookup` | 2cr TikTok, **5cr Instagram**, more with `deep_scan` | the whole batch holds at most **100cr** |
>
> Only successful rows are charged — dead, errored and unsupported rows are refunded, which is
> the genuine benefit. But that is failure insurance, not a bulk discount. **Multiply before
> you send.** Verified live 08.08.26 on the sibling endpoint `POST /youtube/transcripts`:
> 2 ids in, 1 succeeded, `credits_used: 3` — exactly the single-row price, batch or not.

`/comments` at 1cr genuinely beats `instagram/post/comments` or `reddit/post/comments` at 5cr,
and returns the whole thread rather than one page — that one is a flat per-call price.

`/handle-audit` (5cr) projects the data volume and credit cost of pulling a handle *before*
you pull it. Spend it before any large sweep.

### Mid-range reports

`/answers` 15 · `/app-reviews` 15 · `/crisis-radar` 15–45 · `/audience-overlap` 20 ·
`/devtool-pulse` 20 · `/launch-echo` 20 · `/truthsocial-pulse` 20 · `/org-radar` 26

### Big guns — always confirm first

`/demand-signals` 30 · `/reputation` 30 · `/employer-brand` 30 · `/audience-questions` 30 ·
`/product-reviews` 30 · `/apps-lookup` 30 · `/review-integrity` 30 · `/campaign` 35 ·
`/crisis-postmortem` 35 · `/korea-gap` 40 · `/share-of-voice` 40 · `/brand-mentions` 50 ·
`/creator-vet` 50–75 · `/leads` 50

Before booking one of these, check whether a cheap ladder answers the same question:
`/audience-questions` (30cr) versus `reddit/omni-search` (1cr); `/brand-mentions` (50cr)
versus `search/forums` (10cr); `/product-reviews` (30cr) versus two marketplace review calls.
The composites are worth it when you need the fusion and the scoring — not when you need the
raw material.

## `lookup` — real-world caveats (verified live 2026-07-04)

- **Post/detail URLs work best.** A bare profile URL (e.g. `https://www.instagram.com/instagram/`)
  can be rejected `400 INVALID_REQUEST — Unsupported URL` even though the platform is supported —
  the matcher targets post/product/detail link shapes. For profiles, call the platform's
  `profile` endpoint directly (usually 1cr).
- **Supported-link list (from the live 400 message):** TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X/Twitter,
  Facebook, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest, Reddit, Threads, Rumble, Truth Social, GitHub,
  Amazon, Spotify.
- **Transient 502s happen** — upstream resolve can flake; credits auto-refund per the
  UPSTREAM_ERROR policy. Retry once with an `Idempotency-Key`, then fall back to the
  platform-native endpoint.
- Both failure modes cost **0 credits** (pre-flight 400s never deduct; 502s refund).
